habitat: A shy bird of reed beds and thick swamp vegetation. It only occasionally comes out at the edges of pools, and it flicks its tail as it moves.
summary: A fairly common resident. A long red bill and red legs. The identification line says the side of the head and the underparts are grey and the upper parts are rufous. The description says the upper parts are brown and the underparts are barred. The immature is sooty-brown, with the white of the throat extending to the central breast and the flanks barred rufous. The call is a shrill trilling rattle, creeea-crak-crak-crak. The Kemp name African Rail and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Crake is shorter-billed, with a pinkish bill and a red eye. African Rail has a long red bill and red legs.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The upper parts are rufous on the identification line and brown in the description, and the underparts are grey or barred, so those colours are not reduced to one choice. The grade A recording is ND, so the playable file is grade B from Port Alfred. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
